question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III open-ended) has used Valuer X for the last three years for its unlisted-equity positions. Per SEBI's valuation framework amendments, what is the MOST APPROPRIATE next step regarding valuer appointments?

answer.text: Continue Valuer X indefinitely since results have been consistent

Rotate to a new independent valuer on the prescribed rotation cadence and ensure the new entity meets the APMI empanelment and IBBI/Section 247 Registered Valuer Entity eligibility per the September 2024 SEBI Circular
Appoint the fund's auditor as the valuer to save costs
Dispense with external valuation since Valuer X has a long history

explanation.text: The Logic: Independent-valuer eligibility for AIFs broadly requires that the valuer is not an associate of the manager/sponsor/trustee, has the necessary professional credentials (IBBI-registered individual or Registered Valuer Entity under Section 247 of the Companies Act), and rotates periodically so a long-running relationship does not erode independence. Continuing the same valuer indefinitely undermines the independence principle, appointing the fund's own auditor creates a conflict, and dispensing with external valuation is inconsistent with the basic SEBI requirement that unlisted positions be independently valued. The Trap: Continuing Valuer X, appointing the auditor, or dispensing with external valuation each violate the independence/eligibility principles that underlie SEBI's valuation framework. Long history is not a substitute for periodic rotation. Note: The specific rotation cadence, APMI empanelment requirement, and Section 247 framing in the keyed answer reflect general industry/regulatory practice for AIF valuers and are not stated verbatim in the cited workbook chapter (FINAL_Series-XIX-E_Category III AIF Managers.pdf, pp. 338-339 and 350). The framing above is general industry/regulatory knowledge.
